entries.title: Character skill slots: active vs passive
entries.body: Each loadout holds four character skills: one active skill (manually triggered, on a cooldown) and three passives (always on). The EWC 2026 rulebook makes this binding for esports: every player must run an active skill, '1 active, 3 passive' is the allowed format, '4 passive' is prohibited, and no two players on a team may run the same active. Plan the squad's four actives together, for example one wall-breaker, one defensive bubble, one healer and one scan or entry tool, rather than letting each player pick alone. Since Garena's 2023 character rework, character and pet skills no longer have levels and are unlocked with Gold, so every player has the same numbers. Guides that still quote 'level 6' or 'level 8' values describe the old system. The game's preset system saves combos for quick swaps between BR and CS. OB53 added Skill Ban & Pick to CS custom rooms: player 1 bans active skills, then the others pick from what remains.

entries.title: Skill Boost system (OB54)
entries.body: OB54 added Skill Boost alongside Weapon Awakening to give BR matches mid-to-late game growth. A boosted active skill gains an alternative or upgraded effect. Boosts were initially available for Alok, Koda, Homer, Chrono, Kassie, Skyler, Wukong and Oscar, each with two boost options. Examples: Alok 'Speed Remix' widens the aura to 10m with a 16% teammate speed boost. Chrono 'Time Veil' makes the field opaque (still blocks 1000 DMG), while 'Time Drift' makes it move with the user but block only 600 DMG. Skyler's boost 2 searches for Gloo Walls within 75m and locks onto them for 15s. Koda's boost 1 marks enemies revealed in the first detection interval for 3s and shares them. Garena introduced Skill Boost as an event feature, so confirm whether a given tournament lobby enables it before building plans around boosted effects. OB54 also added a once-per-player On-the-Spot Revival in BR.

entries.title: Chrono
entries.body: Active: Time Turner. Creates an impenetrable force field that blocks 1000 DMG. The user cannot shoot enemies outside the field from inside it. Effects last 10s, cooldown 45s (cut from 60s in OB54). It is the default defensive active for holding a revive, crossing open ground in late zones, or buying time when caught without cover, and pro squads typically pair it with a healer such as Alok or Kassie. Because it cannot be shot out of, teach players to use it to reset, not to trade. OB54 Skill Boosts add Time Veil (field becomes opaque, still 1000 DMG) and Time Drift (field moves with the user, blocks 600 DMG). Free Fire Mania lists Chrono among the three most-used competitive characters in 2026; GamsGo ranks it S tier in both BR and CS on OB54.

entries.title: Alok
entries.body: Active: Drop the Beat. Creates an aura around the user that raises movement speed and restores HP to the user and allies inside it; the effect does not stack between multiple Aloks. Third-party guides give 5m radius, +15% movement speed and 5 HP/s for 10s. Garena's current page also describes Party Remix: while the aura is active, music notes lasting 5s drop 2m behind the user every 2s, and teammates who pick one up get the aura effect. OB54 added the Skill Boost Speed Remix (10m aura, 16% teammate speed). Role: support and rotation tempo. Use it to heal after a fight and to speed the squad across open ground into zone. GuruGamer ranks it the top pro-scene character for 2026, and GamsGo ranks it S tier in BR and CS.

entries.body: Active: Electro Therapy. Forms a healing bond with a target teammate that slowly restores HP to both; using the skill again heals the target by a large amount. entries.title: Dimitri
entries.body: Active: Healing Heartbeat. Creates a healing zone where the user and allies recover HP, and downed players inside it can self-revive. That self-revive is what separates it from Alok and Kassie: it saves a knocked teammate when nobody can safely reach them. Guides agree on a 3.5m radius but disagree on healing (see conflicts); BlueStacks and PS Verso give a 60s cooldown. Role: support and clutch-revive. Drop the zone behind cover or a Gloo Wall, because the area is small and anyone standing in it is easy to spray. GamsGo ranks it S tier in BR on OB54, and GuruGamer lists it in the 2026 pro top 10.

entries.title: Oscar
entries.body: Active: Valiant Dash. Dashes in a chosen direction, detonating the first 3 Gloo Walls in the path for 25 DMG each, and deals 25 DMG plus knockback to enemies hit. Cooldown 60s (raised from 45s in OB54). It is the pro scene's go-to aggressive initiator because it opens a walled squad and closes the gap at once. Free Fire Mania names it the most-used competitive character of early 2026. OB54 Skill Boosts: phantom forms extend dash range, or the dash lasts 8s at a speed that builds over time. entries.title: Nero
entries.body: Active: Cryo Mind. Throws a 1-HP plushie that lasts 12s, ignores obstacles and flies up to 50m (100m in BR). It homes on the nearest visible enemy within 8m and bursts into an 8m-radius dreamy space where neither side can place Gloo Walls and enemies lose 6 HP/s. OB55 fixed plushies sticking in the ground. Role: entry and area denial against wall-heavy defenders. Throw it at the squad holding behind walls, then push while they cannot re-wall. entries.title: Ray
entries.body: Active: Bond of Eclipse. Fires a 30m fan forward that tags the first standing enemy hit for 10s and links the two players (the link is visible within 40m only to Ray and the target). If Ray brings the tagged enemy to the knockdown HP threshold, they are knocked instantly. A knock or kill on the tagged target resets the skill and restores 10 HP/s for 3s. Cooldown 45s. Added in OB53. Role: entry fragger, strongest in 1v1 duels. Tag, deal chip damage, and the threshold finishes the knock. New characters are banned for 2 weeks after release in EWC rules, and Ray is on the EWC 2026 allowed list.

entries.title: Morse
entries.body: Active: Stealth Bytes. Enters stealth: hard to see beyond 12m and undetectable by scans, +20% speed and 25 temporary Shield Points, for up to 13s. The user cannot fire while stealthed; exiting has a 0.5s delay. Aim assist triggers on enemies within 12m. Cooldown 45s. Added in OB52 with 15s stealth and a 4m aim-assist trigger. OB55 nerfed it to 13s, with aim assist triggering from 12m. Grenades still work in stealth (TalkEsport). Role: rotation and flank or scout. Use it to cross open ground or reach a third-party angle, then exit early to avoid the 0.5s delay. OB55 makes close-range ambushes harder because enemies' aim assist now catches Morse from 12m.

entries.title: Kenta
entries.body: Active (reworked in OB55): Tempest Raid. Releases a fast forward-moving tempest that passes through Gloo Walls and lasts 8s, dealing 25 DMG to enemies hit. entries.title: Bermuda: overview
entries.body: Bermuda is Free Fire's original island map, released in 2017 alpha, and is still in the competitive pool (it was in the FFWS SEA Spring 2025 pool alongside Purgatory, Alpine, Kalahari and NeXTerra, with Solara added mid-season). It is a compact map with dense villages, rivers with bridges, a central high point at Peak and an outlying island in the south-east (Sentosa). Fights are mostly short and mid range, so AR plus SMG or shotgun is the usual pairing, and circles often pull toward the centre around Peak and Pochinok. The live version at OB55 is the classic Bermuda with Nurek Dam merged in (added from Bermuda Remastered in the OB32 Illuminate update); the separate Bermuda 2.0 / Remastered map was removed from the game in OB54. OB53 to OB55 added event content (Undersea Realm entrance at Nurek Dam, Nine Tails arsenal blasts and loot craters, Peak Mania with more SMGs, shotguns and melee at Peak).

entries.title: Bermuda: Peak
entries.body: Peak is the highest point on Bermuda and sits at the centre of the map, next to Bimasakti Strip and above Pochinok. Loot is spread thin across a few houses and a small number of crates, but height and centrality make it a common final-zone anchor, so it is often contested late rather than early. In OB55 the Peak Mania event adds more SMGs, shotguns and melee weapons to Peak, which turns it into a hot drop for close-range players while the event runs. Risks: open slopes with little cover and exposure to every surrounding town. Rotation exits run downhill in all directions, most commonly to Bimasakti Strip, Pochinok and Factory. In competitive play holding Peak is less about loot and more about controlling the centre circle early.

Rotation exits: east toward Peak and Bimasakti, south to Factory, west to Hangar. Competitive teams that take it usually want to hold the west side of a central zone.

GamingonPhone rates its loot high, while other guides call it a low-risk, medium-loot start. Being a corner, it is quiet early but faces long rotations. OB42 froze its water surface for the winter event. In Bermuda Remastered it was replaced by Aden's Creek, but it is still in classic Bermuda lists. Exits: north to Hangar, east toward Clock Tower and Factory.

data.location: south-west corner (grid B6); near Hangar (north)

entries.title: Bermuda: Sentosa
entries.body: Sentosa is an island in the south-east corner separated from the mainland by a wide river, reached by one bridge or by ziplines from Mars Electric and Kota Tua. It has many houses and platforms and is rated high-tier loot. It was added in June 2019 per Fandom; Bermuda Remastered replaced it with Samurai's Garden, but classic Bermuda keeps it, and OB42 froze its water in the winter event. Risks: the single bridge and zipline approaches become death traps when the zone is on the mainland. Teams who drop here must rotate early.

entries.title: Bermuda: Remastered (Bermuda 2.0) locations
entries.body: Bermuda Remastered, also called Bermuda 2.0, launched with the OB23 update in August 2020 for the 3rd anniversary. It replaced Bullseye and Graveyard with Academy (north-west, between Shipyard and Observatory), Sentosa with Samurai's Garden (south-east island with bridges and ziplines), Rim Nam Village with Aden's Creek (south-west fishing village with scattered shacks), and Plantation and Riverside with Nurek Dam (north of Bimasakti), and reworked Peak with more cover. Only Nurek Dam carried over to classic Bermuda (OB32). OB54 patch notes state 'Removed Bermuda 2.0 and Alpine from the game', so Academy, Aden's Creek and Samurai's Garden are not playable at OB55. Coaches using older VODs should know these names refer to the retired map.

entries.title: Bermuda: rotation routes
entries.body: Bermuda circles very often settle around the centre (Peak, Pochinok, Bimasakti), so the main rotation logic is getting to the middle before the second zone. West-side teams (Hangar, Clock Tower, Observatory, Katulistiwa) move east through Clock Tower and Factory onto Peak; launchers at Observatory and Katulistiwa speed up north-west moves. North teams cross the river at Nurek Dam or the Plantation-Riverside river line, both natural choke points. South-east teams on Sentosa must leave early over the single bridge or the ziplines to Mars Electric and Kota Tua. East teams from Mill and Cape Town face long open runs, so vehicles matter. Guides stress pre-rotating rather than reacting, and using ziplines and rivers for safer crossings.

entries.title: Bermuda: high ground
entries.body: Peak in the centre is the highest point on Bermuda and the key late-game high ground; it has little cover, so holding it means using gloo walls and the houses on the slopes. Observatory in the west is a high spot with a wide view suited to snipers and zone control. The Clock Tower gives vertical sight lines over its town. Keraton is a raised spot over Cape Town in the east. Shipyard cranes and the Factory roof give local height for close fights. Bimasakti Strip's tower overlooks the centre streets, though the strip itself is overlooked by surrounding hills.

entries.title: Purgatory: overview
entries.body: Purgatory is the largest of the three classic maps: a Brazil-inspired island of hills, woods and towns cut by rivers and canals (sources describe it as two or three sections) linked by bridges and ziplines. Bridges are natural choke points, so guides recommend crossing by swimming or vehicle and planning rotations early. Long sightlines favour ARs and snipers over SMGs and shotguns. Key places named in a 2026 guide are Central, Forge, Ski Lodge, Lumber Mill, Golf Course, Mt. Villa and Moathouse; Brasilia and Central are the classic hot drops. Purgatory was in the FFWS SEA Spring 2025 pool. OB55 only touched its Clash Squad minimap; no battle royale layout changes were found in OB53-OB55.

entries.title: NeXTerra: overview
entries.body: NeXTerra launched on 20 August 2022 for Free Fire's 5th anniversary and is a futuristic map made of a main island plus a smaller island at the top, which holds Intellect Center and connects to the mainland by bridges. Its signature mechanics are anti-gravity zones (high jumps, no fall damage, airborne fights, notably at Grav Labs), two-way portals for instant relocation (Deca Square, Intellect Center), ziplines at Zipway and destructible walls and crates (Mud Site). Twelve named locations are commonly listed. Competitively it rewards squads that control portal exits and use gravity zones to flank or disengage; staying airborne too long makes you visible to distant teams. NeXTerra entered the esports pool in 2023, replacing Kalahari, and is in the EWC 2026 pool alongside Bermuda, Purgatory, Kalahari and Solara. Recent patch notes touch it only lightly: OB50 gave it a longer auto-revival window (390s vs 385s on other maps), and OB54 removed the exploit of standing on building edges such as Grav Labs' outer stairs. Official map size was not found.

entries.title: FFWS points system and Champion Rush
entries.body: FFWS-format Battle Royale events score 12 points for a Booyah, then 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 for second through tenth, nothing for 11th and 12th, plus 1 point per kill. Finals use Champion Rush: a team must first reach a points threshold, and only a Booyah won in a later match makes it champion. Reaching the threshold and winning in the same match is not enough, it needs another Booyah. If nobody converts before the match cap, the highest total wins. Thresholds differ by event, so check the rulebook: 80 at FFWS Global Finals 2025 with a 10-match cap, 90 at EWC 2026, and 110 at FFWS SEA 2026 Fall and FFMIC 2026 Fall. Regional finals often use a Point Rush day first that hands out headstart points, for example 10/7/5/3/2/1 for first to sixth at FFMIC 2026 Fall. EWC 2026 tiebreakers go in this order: total Booyahs, total kills, then placement in the last match the tied teams played together.

entries.title: Placement vs kills in league scoring
entries.body: With 1 point per kill and only 12 for a Booyah, kills make up a big share of what top teams score. EVOS took EWC 2025 with 96 kills in 170 total points, more than half their score, and the event write-up described their play as aggressive. LYON's record EWC 2026 game was 33 eliminations plus 12 placement for 45 points, nearly four Booyahs' worth of placement in one match. Even so, placement sets a floor: a 6th-place finish with no fights is still 5 points, and dying early scores nothing. A sound league approach is to take the fights your drop and rotation give you, since early kills add up over a whole league, but never trade a top-five position for a risky kill late on. In Champion Rush, once a team is eligible only the Booyah matters to them. Teams below the threshold should keep farming kills to get there.

entries.title: Edge vs centre play
entries.body: Edge play means rotating along the inside edge of the safe zone with the gas at your back, so enemies can only come at you from the circle side. It also lets you catch teams rotating in late. The cost is that a zone shift away from you forces a long move under fire, and a fight right on the edge can push you into the gas. Centre play gives a short rotation to any next circle, because the new zone usually includes the current centre, but you are exposed from every direction and get third-partied more. Generic guides disagree on which is better, so choose by situation. Go centre when your drop is central, the team has full utility and the next zone is unpredictable. entries.title: Early vs late rotations
entries.body: Rotating early means moving as soon as the next circle shows, or before it shrinks. You get first choice of building or high ground in the new zone and avoid running through teams already set up. The cost is less looting time and the chance of being caught in the open by teams already in position. Rotating late means staying put, looting, and letting other teams fight first. You can then catch weakened teams on the way in, but you may have to cross ground that is already held, take gas damage, and use up Gloo Walls. One guide puts it as rotating just before the shrink, not during it. Another says to estimate travel time the moment a zone finishes closing and move straight away. A late rotation only works if you have a vehicle or plenty of utility. As the zone gets smaller, the damage makes late rotations more costly.

entries.title: Taking a compound
entries.body: Before pushing a building, work out where the enemies are. Use scan skills or an information device, fire to bait a peek, or use sound. entries.title: Holding a compound
entries.body: Holding a building works when you cover several angles and do not give your positions away. Guides suggest finding height inside the building for vision, and using windows to switch angles mid-fight so attackers cannot pre-aim. entries.title: Third-partying: when and how to do it
entries.body: Third-partying means hitting two squads that are already fighting each other. Done well it brings cheap kills, and kills are worth a full point each in league scoring. Hold fire as you approach. Shooting early announces you and can make the two teams stop fighting each other. Wait until both have used utility and taken knocks. The best moment is when they are reviving or looting. Some guides suggest splitting the squad to engage both teams at once. That only works with clear comms, because a split four-stack can be beaten by the winner of the first fight. Before committing, check that you will not be the team caught in the open by a fourth squad, and keep enough Gloo Walls to cover your own retreat. In Champion Rush, third-party the fight that involves an eligible team.

entries.title: Avoiding and surviving third parties
entries.body: You lower the risk of being third-partied by keeping fights short, focusing one target, and finishing knocks fast. Do not start a fight in the open between your team and the next zone. entries.title: Gloo Walls in final zones
entries.body: Final circles are mostly Gloo Wall fights. Place walls before you commit to a fight rather than in panic. Block the specific angle the enemy has on you rather than just your front. Stacking walls vertically gets you onto roofs and high ground. Keep at least one wall in reserve for the last move or a revive. Watch for wall-denial tools. Since OB55, Fireball Jutsu deals 5 damage per second for 5 s to walls, and the CS-only Flame Grenade melts walls for 100 damage every 0.5 s. Nero's field stops wall placement within 8 m. entries.title: Drop strategy in scrims and leagues
entries.body: In organised Brazilian play, a team's chosen landing spot is called its call. Teams usually keep a fixed call over a split so they know the loot, the escape routes and how to share items. LOUD, for example, became known for landing at Shipyard. Breaking the call (quebra de call) means landing on a rival's usual spot on purpose to take away that advantage. It has caused controversy in LBFF and smaller leagues. One team lost its usual Marbleworks drop when several squads landed on it, which helped knock that team out. An ESPN Brasil headline from LBFF 5 quotes Gabriel Reis saying that breaking the call is strategy and part of the game. For a league coach, pick an uncontested drop with good loot and a central or flexible rotation as the default. Plan a backup drop for when you are contested. Contest a rival's drop only when it is worth it in points, for example to slow a leader in a close table. Generic guides warn against drops far from centre that force constant rotation.

entries.title: Comms and calling structure
entries.body: Most squads use one of two calling systems. With named spots, the team agrees names for map features such as specific windows or rooftops and drills them daily. Timing is everything: throw just before you commit, because the effect is short. No OB53, OB54 or OB55 patch note mentions the Flashbang, and no current source found gives its duration or radius. Treat this entry as a description only, and check in-game training for timings before teaching a set play built around it.

entries.title: Jammer
entries.body: The Jammer is a passive anti-scan device. It blocks enemy detection skills and items, such as UAV scans and character scans, without being activated. OB53 added it to the Clash Squad Tactical Market as the anti-scan option when UAV-Lites were removed there. In OB55, devices split into active and passive slots, so a player can carry a Jammer next to an active device such as a UAV-Lite or Launch Pad. OB55 also improved how well it counters detection and added feedback when it blocks a scan. In competitive Battle Royale, where scans are the main way to read the final zones, one Jammer on the player who holds the key spot or flanks can hide where your team really is.

entries.title: Device slots (active and passive)
entries.body: OB55 reworked devices. Before, a player could carry only one device. Now there are active devices (Active Skill Card, Launch Pad, Supply Box, UAV-Lite, Mini Turret, Portal Go) and passive devices (Dragon Sprinters, Jammer, Horizaline), and a player can carry one of each. entries.title: Med Kit and Inhaler
entries.body: Med Kits are the main heal in Battle Royale. Since OB51 players start with 4 Med Kits and 2 Inhalers, and Med Kits no longer take backpack space. OB52 added Med Kits to starter gear and Revival Point kits (6 Med Kits). OB53 set the Inhaler carry limit to 10, cut Med Kits in coin machines from 2 to 1, and made sprinting into a heal stop the sprint and start healing. OB54 removed Med Kits from Coin Machines and increased ground drops. OB55 lets players help a teammate up without interrupting Med Kit use. Healing is no longer the bottleneck it was. Coach point: heal behind Gloo Walls between fights and stop tracking heal counts closely, but keep Inhalers for repeek duels.

entries.title: Revival
entries.body: Battle Royale has several ways to bring back eliminated teammates. Capturing a Revival Point revives them. OB55 revives them from stone coffins at the point with brief protection and revival supplies instead of parachuting them in. OB50 cut the Revival Point cooldown from 300 to 180 s, and from OB51 all points upgrade to Advanced Revival Points at 420 s. Revive Cards can be bought until 355 s (OB54, down from 420 s). OB54 also added On-the-Spot Revival: each player can be revived where they fell once, it takes 10 s and is unavailable after the 4th Safe Zone. OB52 added a one-time team early revival with a 60 s countdown. OB55 cut the Solo revival window from 540 to 410 s. Capturing the Ultra Airdrop also revives teammates. EWC 2026 rules keep revival on.

entries.title: Airdrops
entries.body: OB55 set Battle Royale airdrops to a fixed schedule. Regular Airdrops start at around 160 s, with 4 per match. Two Defense Airdrops land together at 410 s. One Ultra Airdrop lands at around 410 s; capturing it gives Lv. 5 armour and revives eliminated teammates. Minimap markers disappear once an airdrop has been outside the zone for 45 s. Because the 410 s drops come at known times, plan rotations around them: contest them only when the drop is near your path to the zone.

entries.title: How the zone closes
entries.body: Each Battle Royale Safe Zone phase has a countdown before the shrink, then a shrink that takes a set time. The current Solo timings for Bermuda, Kalahari, Purgatory and Alpine in OB52 have 7 zones. Zone 1 has a 90 s countdown and a 165 s shrink. Countdowns are 50 s for zones 2-3, 30 s for zone 4, 20 s for zone 5 and 10 s for zones 6-7. Shrinks take 85, 75, 70, 60, 60 and 90 s. NeXTerra Solo has 6 zones, and its first zone appears 50 s into the match. OB49 enlarged NeXTerra's early zones (450, 225 and 115 m) and lengthened the Squad zone 1 countdown on all maps to 140 s. OB55 changed Solara's shrink timing to match the other maps without publishing numbers. Damage grows each phase, so late rotations through the zone cost more and more HP. EWC 2026 rules play with Safe Zone Moving on.

entries.title: M7
entries.body: The M7 is a new fully automatic assault rifle added in OB55 on 2026-10-01, built for mid-to-long range. It uses Garena's new recoil system: instead of the usual random bullet spread, recoil steadily pulls the aim upward while firing, so it is learnable and can be pulled down. IDC/Games notes skilled players can start the burst at the torso and let the climb carry rounds to the head. In BR it is rare ground loot in high-tier zones and arsenals; IDC/Games reports vending machines selling it for 400 FF Coins; in Clash Squad it costs 1600 CS Cash. entries.title: AWM
entries.body: The AWM is the benchmark bolt-action sniper: top damage and range bars, 5-round magazine, slow reload, pre-equipped 8x scope. OB53 gave it +20% armor penetration and +50% limb damage, compensating for the removal of the global limb multiplier, so limb and body hits now hit hard through armor. OB55 cut both movement speed and movement speed while firing by 8%, in line with Garena's stated goal that snipers punish openings rather than win quick peek fights. Since OB54 it no longer spawns from Arsenals in BR; in OB55 it is bought from Vending Machines for 600 FF Coins (limit 3 per match). Coaching use: give it to the squad's designated long-range player, hold angles from cover or high ground, and avoid repositioning while scoped. Muzzle and suppressor are the slots that matter; extended magazine helps the slow reload.

entries.body: The M14 (with upgradeable M14-I to M14-III) is a marksman rifle with the highest rate-of-fire bar and the largest magazine (15) in its class but the lowest damage bar. OB55 nerfed movement speed -5% and movement speed while firing -5%, the lightest marksman nerf. Role: forgiving mid-range poke for players who miss single shots; less burst than SVD or Woodpecker.

entries.title: OB55 sniper and marksman mobility nerf
entries.body: OB55 (BR from 2026-10-01) cut movement for every sniper and marksman rifle. Garena's stated intent: snipers keep their fight-ending damage but should capitalise on openings instead of relying on mobility for quick peeks; marksman rifles keep accuracy and armor penetration with faster follow-up shots. Changes: AWM and Kar98k -8% movement and firing movement; M82B and M24 -10% firing movement; VSK94 -15% movement and -10% firing movement; M14 -5%/-5%; Winchester -5%/-7% plus -60% extra damage to armor; SKS, SVD and Woodpecker -5%/-12%; AC80 -5%/-17%. OB54 had already added a global movement speed cap. Coaching takeaway: snipers should pre-position before fights and stop jiggle-peeking while scoped.

entries.title: Attachment system overview
entries.body: BR attachments are looted and fit fixed slots: muzzle (adds range; levels 1-3), silencer/suppressor (removes minimap and sound alerts when firing), magazine (more rounds and faster reload; levels 1-3, plus double magazine), foregrip (recoil reduction; levels 1-3), stock (stability and movement while firing; levels 1-3) and scopes (2x, 4x, 8x, thermal). Some weapons also had weapon-specific attachments, for example Armor Piercer on AWM or Rage Core on M14, but the only source for these is from 2021, so check them in game before coaching on them. Slots are fixed per gun and Garena changes them in patch notes: OB53 added a muzzle slot to UMP and to M590 (no silencer), a foregrip to Charge Buster, and foregrip plus stock to PLASMA and Kord. The OB51 loadout rework replaced loadouts with Team Booster slots and Super Leg Pockets rather than weapon attachments, and no current source shows Armory attachments carrying into BR.

entries.title: Attachment slots by weapon class (snipers and marksman)
entries.body: Long guns have restricted slots. Bolt-action snipers mostly take muzzle and suppressor only: Free Fire Mania lists Kar98k and M82B as suppressor plus muzzle, and both AWM and Kar98k come with an 8x scope that cannot be swapped. Its AWM page also lists foregrip and magazine. The pre-OB53 M24 took foregrip, stock and muzzle. Marksman rifles are more flexible: SVD takes foregrip, stock, magazine, suppressor and muzzle, and the AC80 takes foregrip, stock, suppressor, scope and muzzle but no magazine. BlueStacks names scope and muzzle as the key sniper attachments, since muzzle extends effective range. For snipers, prioritise muzzle, then suppressor, so long shots do not reveal position on the minimap. For marksman rifles, add a foregrip and stock to tighten follow-up shots, now that OB55 has cut their movement while firing. By contrast, SMGs and shotguns get slots such as the muzzle added to UMP and M590 in OB53.

entries.title: Armor: vests, helmets and damage reduction
entries.body: Helmets and vests come in levels and lose durability as they absorb damage. NamuWiki (revised 2026-06) lists helmet Lv1/2/3 at 33/50/66% damage reduction with 70/155/240 durability, and vest Lv1/2/3 at 33/50/66% with 190/225/260 durability. A Lv4 vest (290 durability) comes from airdrops or armor upgrades, and damaged versions block less. OB53 removed the limb damage multiplier, so limb hits now do the same damage as body shots, and armor now covers limbs. At the same time snipers got +50% limb damage and +20% armor penetration. OB54 changed BR Arsenals: Basic gives 2 Lv2 sets plus 2 Lv3 sets, Upgraded gives 4 Lv3 sets. Armor penetration varies by weapon (Woodpecker and M82B highest among long guns), and OB55 cut the Winchester's extra damage to armor by 60%. Coaching takeaway: squads should leave Arsenals in Lv3 armor, and long-gun picks should favour armor penetration.
